planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun, where strong light develops the densest spotting.

directions: Jaguar is one of the original wave of Mangave hybrids to popularize the group, its broad grey-green rosette densely stippled in maroon-purple flecks that thicken toward near-solid coloring under strong sun and drought stress. The soft, rubbery leaf tips lack the rigid terminal spine of true agave, making it far more forgiving to handle in a border or container planting. It combines Manfreda's quick, offsetting growth and tolerance of regular garden watering with Agave's tidy rosette form, reaching flowering size in a few years rather than the decades a true century plant requires. Several later color sports, including the yellow-margined Kaleidoscope, trace their spotted patterning back to this parent plant.

common_name: New Big Dwarf Tomato (Heirloom Potato-Leaf Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; the sturdy, potato-leaf dwarf habit needs only light staking and suits raised beds and large containers.

directions: New Big Dwarf was introduced by the Livingston Seed Company in 1917 as an improvement on earlier dwarf tomato lines, combining a compact, potato-leaf, non-sprawling habit with unusually large fruit for its class. Mature pink beefsteak-type tomatoes can approach a pound, with smooth shoulders and rich, well-balanced flavor on plants short enough to grow without a full cage. Its early-20th-century dwarf, rugose-leaved genetics made it a natural choice for modern hybridizers, and it stands behind later Dwarf Tomato Project crosses, including as a parent of Tasmanian Chocolate alongside Paul Robeson. Harvest as fruit fully colors and softens slightly at the blossom end for best flavor.

common_name: Golden Dwarf Champion Tomato (Heirloom Yellow Potato-Leaf Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; the compact, rugose-leafed dwarf habit needs only light staking.

directions: Golden Dwarf Champion is a yellow-fruited sport of the 19th-century heirloom Dwarf Champion tomato, one of the earliest true dwarf, potato-leaf tomato lines grown in American gardens. Plants stay short and self-supporting while producing round to oblate golden-yellow fruit with a mild, sweet flavor typical of yellow heirloom tomatoes. Along with other old dwarf lines, it was preserved by seed savers into the era of the modern Dwarf Tomato Project, where its compact genetics have been bred into newer releases such as Dwarf Sweet Sue, crossed with Green Giant. Harvest as fruit turns fully golden and softens slightly for peak sweetness.

common_name: Budai Torpe Tomato (Hungarian Heirloom Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; the short, rugose-leafed dwarf habit needs little to no staking.

directions: Budai Torpe, whose Hungarian name translates roughly to 'Buda dwarf,' is a compact, potato-leaf heirloom tomato from Hungary grown for generations before it entered wider international seed exchange. Its thick, rugose foliage and short, self-supporting stems are typical of old-world dwarf tomato lines, and it bears medium-sized red fruit with a brisk, well-balanced flavor. Along with other historic dwarf varieties, it was folded into the founding gene pool of the modern Dwarf Tomato Project, most notably crossed with Black From Tula to produce the early-maturing Dwarf Arctic Rose. Harvest as fruit ripens fully on the vine.
